# Commit multi-workspace dock transactions atomically

## Context

`WorkspaceDocument.commit()` already returns before/after truth for one participant. D#18224 kept it pure and moved transaction ownership upward: a Group must coordinate every affected Workspace and placement participant without coupling the model to managers or native windows.

## The Problem

A multi-window operation currently has no single serialized commit. Sequential writes can leave one Workspace updated when a later adoption fails; moving a cursor before durable truth or recording requested window effects invents history. The current InstanceService undo path also partially replays before a structured refusal.

## The Architectural Reality

The Group owns the queue and transaction boundary; participants own pure prepare/adopt/compensate operations. Semantic document truth commits before projection. Native open/move/close is not ACID and records a separate observed-effect receipt. Mode is two axes: `cursorAction = append | preserve | undo | redo` plus provenance/cause.

## The Fix

Implement the six-step Group write: capture and prepare all at the queue head; adopt all with reverse-order compensation; append the immutable row; move cursor; publish one current topology snapshot; release the queue. Capture participant generations/revisions with their values, prebuild recursively frozen payloads, and recheck generations/revisions immediately before synchronous, effect-free adoption. Compensation covers every invoked adopter, including one that mutates before throwing, and any fallible history/cursor update. Publish notifications only after the semantic state is consistent. Projection and effect receipts run after the semantic write. Cold hydrate preserves cursor state, user restore appends, warm rebind writes nothing, undo/redo append nothing. Reject mixed dock/non-dock batches until compensation covers both.

## Decision Record impact

Implements amended ADR 0029's semantic-commit-before-effect rule.

## Decision Record

Required prerequisite: the #18303 hard-cut authority leaf.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns criterion 8 and the transaction boundary in criteria 1/7.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every participant prepares before any adoption; a prepare refusal leaves all participants, history, cursor, and snapshot unchanged.
- [ ] A failure on adoption N compensates every invoked participant in reverse order, including N if it mutated before throwing. Inject that second-participant failure: all participant truth, history membership, cursor, and snapshot remain byte-identical, with no publication or projection.
- [ ] Successful order is exactly prepare → adopt/compensate → append row → cursor → snapshot → queue release; participant adoption is synchronous and performs no presentation or native effect.
- [ ] A failed write rejects observably but does not poison the next queued write.
- [ ] `append`, `preserve`, `undo`, and `redo` semantics match their no-extra-row rules and carry explicit provenance/cause.
- [ ] Projection/effect receipts cannot make a semantic commit appear failed or invent a commit after semantic refusal.
- [ ] Mixed dock/non-dock batches are structurally rejected until cross-domain compensation is present; pure dock origins share this path.
- [ ] With two queued calls and a delayed first prepare, B captures A's committed after-state at its own queue head. A generation/revision change before adoption refuses before a stale write.
- [ ] Inject a history-append or cursor-update failure after participant adoption: compensate the participant and history/cursor changes, preserve the previous snapshot, emit no committed snapshot event, and allow the next queued write to run.
- [ ] History and Group observers first see recursively frozen rows and consistent participant/history/cursor/snapshot state. A synchronous listener that reads state and enqueues another operation cannot observe an intermediate commit; a notification failure is reported separately and cannot turn an already published semantic commit into a refusal.

## Out of Scope

Geometry quiescence, command/UI wiring, topology parser changes, or cross-Group two-phase commit.

## Avoided Traps

No recording inside WorkspaceDocument; no Promise fan-out of state writes; no cursor-first update; no requested-effect fiction; no swallowed failure tail.

## Related

Part of #18303. Blocked by Group binding and immutable history. Enables topology projection and undo migration.

Detailed source contract and failure controls: [Emmy's D#18224 transaction protocol](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18224#discussioncomment-18292268). Existing primitives include the Collection update bracket and Provider effect batching; `collection.Base#splice` / `core.Observable#fire` dispatch synchronously, so frozen-after-return alone is insufficient.
